per-vīvo , xi, ctum, 3, v. n.,
I.to live on, survive to a certain time (ante-class.): pervixi usque adhuc, Att. ap. Non. 238, 2 (Trag. Rel. v. 417 Rib.): “pervivo usque ad summam aetatem,” Plaut. Capt. 3, 5, 84 .
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
